title.en: What Kind of Impossible Café Would You Open?
title.zh: 你会开一家怎样的不可能咖啡馆？

description.en: Design an imaginary café where visitors exchange tiny performances, borrowed words or invented colors. Six choices shape its unusual invitation.
description.zh: 设计一间交换小表演、借来文字或新造颜色的虚构咖啡馆，六个选择决定特别邀请。

introduction.en: No real business plan, menu expertise or purchase is involved. You are inventing a place with one playful rule. The result concerns the experience you designed, not career suitability or entrepreneurial ability.
introduction.zh: 不做真实商业计划，不需菜单知识或购买。你只为虚构场所创一条趣味规则。结果谈设计的体验，不评职业适合或创业能力。

focus.en: Offering visitors a tiny stage, a shared language experiment or a way to make something visually new.
focus.zh: 给访客一个小舞台、共享文字实验或造出新视觉的机会。

prompt.zh: 咖啡馆的不可能特色是……

label.en: Each empty saucer can become a miniature stage.
label.zh: 每个空碟都能变迷你舞台。

label.en: Visitors can borrow a sentence and return it changed.
label.zh: 访客可借一句话，改写后归还。

label.en: Guests can mix a color that has no name yet.
label.zh: 客人能调一种还没名字的颜色。

prompt.en: A newcomer does not want to participate. You offer…

label.en: A sentence to read privately without returning anything.
label.zh: 一句可私读、不必还的文字。

label.en: A place to watch colors without having to make one.
label.zh: 只看颜色、不必动手的位置。

label.en: A seat where watching counts as the whole visit.
label.zh: 看表演便算完整到访的座位。

prompt.en: A regular leaves one contribution. It is…

label.en: A tiny swatch with an invented and changeable name.
label.zh: 一块新色样，名字随时可改。

label.en: A ten-second scene made from ordinary table objects.
label.zh: 普通桌物演的十秒小戏。

label.en: A new ending to a sentence someone left earlier.
label.zh: 给前人一句话换的新结尾。

prompt.en: The café needs one house rule. You choose…

label.en: Anyone can leave a scene before its final bow.
label.zh: 任何人都可在谢幕前离开。

label.en: A borrowed sentence must remain open to another version.
label.zh: 借来的句子须容得下另一版。

label.en: Nobody has to agree on the name of a new shade.
label.zh: 不必人人同意新色叫什么。

prompt.en: The room is empty at closing. What remains?

label.en: A few phrases ready for different readers tomorrow.
label.zh: 几句话等明天不同读者。

label.en: One little stage waiting for a new ordinary object.
label.zh: 一个小舞台等新普通物登场。

label.en: A changing palette without a compulsory final picture.
label.zh: 变动色盘，不强求最终画作。

prompt.en: The invitation on the door says…

label.en: Make a shade the world has not named here yet.
label.zh: 在这里调出世界未起名的一色。

label.en: Borrow a line and see what happens to it.
label.zh: 借一句话，看看会变什么。

label.en: Let a small everyday thing take the stage.
label.zh: 让日常小东西上一次台。

summary.en: Your café makes ordinary things briefly perform. A spoon or paper scrap can become a character without the visitor needing to be an actor or the audience needing to applaud.
summary.zh: 你的馆让普通物短暂演出。匙或纸片可当角色，访客不必会演，观众不必鼓掌。

example.en: A folded receipt might sail across a saucer while its maker gives it one line about searching for the edge of the table.
example.zh: 折收据驶过碟子，作者给它一句寻找桌边的台词。

strength.en: A tiny stage gives playful expression a clear, manageable frame and lets an everyday object be seen differently for a short visit.
strength.zh: 小舞台给表达清晰可控的框，让日常物在短到访中被换种眼光看。

tradeoff.en: Even a tiny performance can feel exposing. Your imagined café works best when watching, declining and stopping midway remain complete ways to visit.
tradeoff.zh: 再小表演也可能怕被看。观看、拒绝和中途停下都算完整到访，馆才好玩。

experiment.en: Give one harmless object a two-line scene on a drawn saucer. End the performance while it is still small enough to enjoy.
experiment.zh: 在画的碟子上，给一件无害物写两句戏，仍小到有趣时就收场。

summary.en: Your invented place lets language travel between visitors. A sentence is a shared starting point rather than a test of who writes the cleverest or most revealing response.
summary.zh: 你的场所让文字在访客间走动。句子是共享起点，不考谁写得最聪明或最袒露。

example.en: A card saying “the cupboard opened onto Tuesday” might return tomorrow with a new ending and an entirely different imagined cupboard.
example.zh: 写“柜门打开就是星期二”的卡片，明天可换结尾，柜子也全不同。

strength.en: Borrowing a line lowers the size of the blank page and gives strangers an indirect, optional way to contribute to the same fiction.
strength.zh: 借一句话缩小空白页，让陌生人间接且自愿参与同一虚构。

tradeoff.en: A sentence can be misunderstood or changed in a way its first writer dislikes. Fictional contributions should be offered only when that openness is welcome.
tradeoff.zh: 句子可能被误读或改得作者不喜。只有欢迎开放改写时，才把虚构贡献放出。

experiment.en: Write one clearly fictional sentence and make two different endings yourself. Notice how the same beginning can support incompatible but enjoyable stories.
experiment.zh: 写一句明确虚构的话，自写两种结尾，看看同一开头如何容纳相异有趣故事。

title.zh: 还没起名的颜色咖啡馆

summary.en: Your café invites visitors to make a visual possibility before explaining it. A new shade can exist without one correct name, a polished picture or a message about personality.
summary.zh: 你的馆邀请先造视觉可能，再解释。新颜色可没有唯一正名、精画或人格寓意。

example.en: A guest might imagine mixing pale blue with the color of a remembered ticket and call the result “almost boarding.”
example.zh: 客人可想象浅蓝混记忆中票根色，叫它“快登车了”。

strength.en: An unnamed palette gives small visual experiments room to remain provisional, so trying a combination need not become a claim about artistic talent.
strength.zh: 无名色盘让小实验可暂定，试配色不变成画技主张。

tradeoff.en: Invented colors may be difficult to describe accessibly. A short text description can let another visitor enjoy the idea without relying on sight alone.
tradeoff.zh: 新色可能难描述。添短文字，让他人不只靠视觉也能享受想法。

experiment.en: Invent a harmless color name and describe it in ordinary words, including an imagined texture or setting. No actual materials or purchases are needed.
experiment.zh: 造无害色名，用普通话描述，带一种想象质地或场景，不需材料购买。

topic.zh: 不可能咖啡馆设计测试

title.zh: 不可能咖啡馆设计测试

description.en: Invent a cafe with saucer stages, borrowed sentences or unnamed colors. Six creative choices reveal the experience your imaginary place offers its visitors.
description.zh: 发明有碟子舞台、可借句子或无名颜色的咖啡馆。六次创作选择，看看想象场所给访客怎样的体验。

question.en: Does this cafe quiz test whether I should open a business?
question.zh: 咖啡馆测试，会判断我是否该开店吗？

answer.en: You are choosing one playful rule for a fictional place, not preparing a business plan. A tiny stage, a language exchange and color-making invite different activities without implying commercial demand or entrepreneurial skill.
answer.zh: 你在给虚构场所选趣味规则，不做商业计划。小舞台、文字交换和调色邀请不同活动，不意味着市场需求或创业技能。
